analysis.title: Up and Adam (Investment Strategy daily, Thursday, October 8, 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 Industrials fell 2.1% on Wednesday and is down 9.9% from its August record high, near correction territory. Aerospace and defense stocks are down 20% on concern over US defense spending, as expectations rise for a Democratic-controlled Congress after the midterms.
Transports are down 12% with diesel and jet fuel prices near multi-year highs. Raymond James remains positive on Industrials, citing the AI buildout, electric grid modernization and reshoring.
The Stoxx Europe 600 is down about 8% in USD terms from its August record high on investor concern over France's public debt. The euro is down about 4% against the dollar YTD.

The S&P 500 sits just below Tuesday's all-time high, so Europe trails the US by about 12%, the widest performance gap of the year. Raymond James favors the US and Japan over Europe on stronger earnings growth and technology leadership.
The $39 billion 10-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.30%, the highest yield since 2000 but 1.7 bps below prevailing market levels. Bid-to-cover was 2.77, the highest since January 2016.

Indirect bidders, a proxy for foreign demand, took 80% of the 10-year auction. Dealers were left with 2.5%, a record low for a 10-year auction. Raymond James reads this as robust demand for US Treasuries at multi-decade high yields. A $22 billion 30-year auction follows today.

In the NY Fed's September Survey of Consumer Expectations, one-year inflation expectations rose 30 bps to 3.9%, the highest since May 2023. Three-year expectations rose 10 bps to 3.3% and five-year expectations held at 3.0%.
Perceived risk of job loss fell to its lowest level since Dec. 2024. Raymond James says anchored longer-term expectations should give the Fed confidence to hold rates at the Oct. 27-28 meeting.

The Russell 2000 is down 9% from its Aug. 14 record high amid the jump in bond yields. It broke below an uptrend line in place since the April 2025 Liberation Day lows, with the 200-day moving average the next near-term support. Raymond James continues to favor large-caps for diversified revenue, stronger margins, supply-chain flexibility and lower sensitivity to borrowing costs.
